content.text:
**OpenAI has shifted its focus to a code-first, production-oriented agent ecosystem centered on the Responses API and the Agents SDK.**[[1]](https://ecorpit.com/openai-agent-api-selection-responses-agents-sdk-agentkit-2026/)

### Key Recent Updates (2025–2026)
- **March 2025**: OpenAI introduced the **Responses API** (a superset of Chat Completions that adds built-in tools like web search, file search, and computer use) and the **Agents SDK** for orchestrating single- and multi-agent workflows. It also added integrated observability (tracing), guardrails, sessions, and realtime/voice capabilities. The older Assistants API was slated for eventual deprecation (now set for August 26, 2026).[[2]](https://openai.com/index/new-tools-for-building-agents/)

- **October 2025**: Launch of **AgentKit**, which included Agent Builder (a visual canvas for workflows), ChatKit (embeddable UI), Connector Registry, and Evals tools. These were positioned for building, deploying, and optimizing agents.[[3]](https://openai.com/index/introducing-agentkit/)

- **April 2026**: Major update to the **Agents SDK** with enterprise-focused safety and capability improvements, including:
  - Native sandbox execution (isolated workspaces for file/code access while protecting the broader system).
  - In-distribution harness for frontier models, supporting file operations, code editing, shell tools, and long-running tasks.
  - Features like MCP tools, skills (gradual information disclosure), AGENTS.md for custom instructions, and apply-patch for file edits.
  - Initial Python support, with TypeScript following; standard API pricing applies.[[4]](https://techcrunch.com/2026/04/15/openai-updates-its-agents-sdk-to-help-enterprises-build-safer-more-capable-agents/)

- **June 2026 Deprecations** (announced June 3):
  - **Assistants API** (`/v1/assistants` and `/v1/threads`): Fully sunsets August 26, 2026 — calls will error with no grace period. Migrate to Responses API + Conversations API.[[1]](https://ecorpit.com/openai-agent-api-selection-responses-agents-sdk-agentkit-2026/)
  - **Agent Builder** (visual canvas in AgentKit) and **Evals platform**: Both shut down November 30, 2026 (Evals becomes read-only October 31). Reusable prompt objects are also removed. Recommendation: Rebuild logic in the Agents SDK (code-first) or use Workspace Agents in ChatGPT for natural-language prompting. ChatKit and the Responses API remain fully supported.[[5]](https://pickaxe.co/post/openai-agent-builder-deprecation)

- **Ongoing (as of mid-2026)**: The **Responses API** is now OpenAI’s flagship primitive for new agent projects. It supports multi-agent workflows (beta as of 2026, allowing a root agent to spawn parallel subagents for tasks like codebase exploration). The Agents SDK is production-ready (evolved from the experimental Swarm framework), with releases up to v0.17+ and features like tool search, computer-use GA, sessions, tracing, and hosted tools.[[6]](https://platform.openai.com/docs/llms-full.txt)

### Current Recommendations (Late 2026)
- For new agent development: Start with the **Responses API** (own the loop, direct control) or the **Agents SDK** (SDK manages orchestration, ideal for typed code in Python/TypeScript).[[6]](https://platform.openai.com/docs/llms-full.txt)
- Avoid starting new projects on Assistants API or Agent Builder.
- Documentation and SDKs are available on GitHub (openai-agents-python, openai-agents-js) and the OpenAI developer platform.[[7]](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/llms.txt)

This represents a clear move away from visual/low-code builders toward robust, observable, sandboxed code-based agents. For the latest official details, check the OpenAI platform docs or the Agents SDK release notes, as features like multi-agent and sandboxing continue to evolve.
